This commit includes significant progress on a major UI/UX overhaul aimed at creating a professional, clean, and modern Nordstrom-branded analytics dashboard.

Summary of changes:

**Phase 1: Foundational Setup & Global Styles (Completed)**
- Defined Nordstrom primary color (`#004170` - Navy Blue) as `nordstrom-blue` in `tailwind.config.js`.
- Integrated the 'Inter' font as the default application font.
- Applied global styling: light gray background (`#F7F8FA`) for the body, ensured `box-sizing: border-box`.
- Resolved potential background conflicts from `App.css`.
- Updated `Layout.tsx` for improved content structure (`max-w-7xl`, `mx-auto`).

**Phase 2: Navigation (Completed)**
- Redesigned `Header.tsx`: Switched to a light theme (`bg-white`), styled title with `nordstrom-blue`, and adapted interactive elements. Ensured sticky positioning.
- Redesigned `Sidebar.tsx`: Maintained a light theme, updated link styling for hover and active states using `nordstrom-blue`, and replaced emojis with Heroicons for navigation items, header logo, and theme toggle. Improved label clarity and layout.

**Phase 3: Card & Component Redesign (In Progress - Steps 7 & 8 Completed)**
- **Upgraded KPI Cards & Sections:**
    - KPI stat cards in `DashboardOverview.tsx` (Total Posts, Likes, etc.) and dedicated `InstagramEngagementCard.tsx` & `TikTokEngagementCard.tsx` were restyled to a consistent modern card design (`bg-white dark:bg-gray-700/800`, `rounded-xl`, `shadow-lg`, `p-6`) with `nordstrom-blue` for key figures and icons. Old gradient backgrounds were removed.
    - Main analytical section wrappers in `DashboardOverview.tsx` (Sentiment, Engagement, Reach, Hashtag sections), the "Quick Stats" card, and all chart sections at the bottom of the page now also use this new elevated card styling.
    - The internal structure of `SentimentAnalysis.tsx`, `EngagementSection.tsx`, `ReachSection.tsx`, and `HashtagSection.tsx` was refactored to remove conflicting styles and fit cleanly within their new card containers, with standardized internal titles and elements.
- **Button Styling:**
    - Platform Toggle Buttons (MUI `ToggleButtonGroup`) in `DashboardOverview.tsx` were restyled to use `nordstrom-blue` for selected states and have a consistent professional appearance across all sections.
    - Action buttons in `Header.tsx` (e.g., "Filters", "Export Data") were styled as "Outline Buttons" using `nordstrom-blue`. The main "Refresh Data" button uses a solid `nordstrom-blue` background. Icon buttons (Dark Mode, Mobile Menu) were also refined.

**Next Steps (Not included in this commit):**
- Phase 3 (cont.): Styling form controls (dropdowns).
- Phase 4: Redesigning all charts and graphs.
- Phase 5: Comprehensive responsiveness testing and final polish.

This work aims to significantly enhance the visual appeal and professionalism of the application.

Updating ovn-kubernetes-microshift-container image to be consistent with ART for 4.18
__TLDR__:
Product builds by ART can be configured for different base and builder images than corresponding CI
builds. This automated PR requests a change to CI configuration to align with ART's configuration;
please take steps to merge it quickly or contact ART to coordinate changes.

The configuration in the following ART component metadata is driving this alignment request:
[ovn-kubernetes-microshift.yml](https://github.com/openshift/ocp-build-data/tree/8a8c11ba2c7cf69068d75bd84a096a7cdcd1872f/images/ovn-kubernetes-microshift.yml).

__Detail__:

This repository is out of sync with the downstream product builds for this component. The CI
configuration for at least one image differs from ART's expected product configuration. This should
be addressed to ensure that the component's CI testing accurate reflects what customers will
experience.

Most of these PRs are opened as an ART-driven proposal to migrate base image or builder(s) to a
different version, usually prior to GA. The intent is to effect changes in both configurations
simultaneously without breaking either CI or ART builds, so usually ART builds are configured to
consider CI as canonical and attempt to match CI config until the PR merges to align both. ART may
also configure changes in GA releases with CI remaining canonical for a brief grace period to enable
CI to succeed and the alignment PR to merge. In either case, ART configuration will be made
canonical at some point (typically at branch-cut before GA or release dev-cut after GA), so it is
important to align CI configuration as soon as possible.

PRs are also triggered when CI configuration changes without ART coordination, for instance to
change the number of builder images or to use a different golang version. These changes should be
coordinated with ART; whether ART configuration is canonical or not, preferably it would be updated
first to enable the changes to occur simultaneously in both CI and ART at the same time. This also
gives ART a chance to validate the intended changes first. For instance, ART compiles most
components with the Golang version being used by the control plane for a given OpenShift release.
Exceptions to this convention (i.e. you believe your component must be compiled with a Golang
version independent from the control plane) must be granted by the OpenShift staff engineers and
communicated to the ART team.

__Roles & Responsibilities__:
- Component owners are responsible for ensuring these alignment PRs merge with passing
  tests OR that necessary metadata changes are reported to the ART team: `@release-artists`
  in `#forum-ocp-art` on Slack. If necessary, the changes required by this pull request can be
  introduced with a separate PR opened by the component team. Once the repository is aligned,
  this PR will be closed automatically.
- In particular, it could be that a job like `verify-deps` is complaining. In that case, please open
  a new PR with the dependency issues addressed (and base images bumped). [ART-9595](https://issues.redhat.com//browse/ART-9595) for reference.
- Patch-manager or those with sufficient privileges within this repository may add
  any required labels to ensure the PR merges once tests are passing. In cases where ART config is
  canonical, downstream builds are *already* being built with these changes, and merging this PR
  only improves the fidelity of our CI. In cases where ART config is not canonical, this provides
  a grace period for the component team to align their CI with ART's configuration before it becomes
  canonical in product builds.

ART has been configured to reconcile your CI build root image (see https://docs.ci.openshift.org/docs/architecture/ci-operator/#build-root-image).
In order for your upstream .ci-operator.yaml configuration to be honored, you must set the following in your openshift/release ci-operator configuration file:
```
build_root:
  from_repository: true
```

__Change behavior of future PRs__:
* In case you just want to follow the base images that ART suggests, you can configure additional labels to be
  set up automatically. This means that such a PR would *merge without human intervention* (and awareness!) in the future.
  To do so, open a PR to set the `auto_label` attribute in the image configuration. [Example](https://github.com/openshift-eng/ocp-build-data/pull/1778)
* You can set a commit prefix, like `UPSTREAM: <carry>: `. [An example](https://github.com/openshift-eng/ocp-build-data/blob/6831b59dddc5b63282076d3abe04593ad1945148/images/ose-cluster-api.yml#L11).

This PR implements comprehensive CI/CD automation with multi-architecture Docker builds to support both x86_64 and ARM64 platforms, addressing the mixed-architecture Kubernetes cluster setup described in the blog content.

## 🚀 Features Added

### Multi-Architecture Docker Builds
- **Platforms**: Automated builds for `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64`
- **Registry**: Images published to GitHub Container Registry (`ghcr.io/skill-wanderer/blog-v2`)
- **Optimization**: Docker Buildx with GitHub Actions caching for faster builds
- **Tagging**: Smart tagging strategy (latest, branch names, PR numbers, semantic versions)

**1. Build and Push (`build-and-push.yml`)**
- Multi-architecture Docker builds on push to main/master
- GitHub Container Registry integration
- Conditional pushing (PRs only build, pushes build + push)
- Build summaries with platform and tag information

**2. Continuous Integration (`ci.yml`)**
- Validates npm build process
- Tests Docker build functionality
- Uploads build artifacts
- Runs on all pushes and PRs

**3. Dependency Management (`dependency-update.yml`)**
- Weekly automated dependency updates
- Creates PRs with security fixes

```bash
docker pull ghcr.io/skill-wanderer/blog-v2:latest
```

Both architectures can now pull and run the same image tag, enabling seamless deployment across the Kubernetes cluster.

Add a new `brew mcp-server` command for a [Model Context Protocol (MCP)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/introduction) server for Homebrew. This integrates with AI/LLM tools like Claude, Claude Code and Cursor.

It currently supports the calls needed/used by the [MCP Inspector](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/tools/inspector) and Cursor (where I've tested it).

It provides as `tools` the subcommands output by `brew help` but should be fairly straightforward to add more in future.

It is implemented in a slightly strange way (a standalone Ruby command called from a shell command) as MCP servers need a faster startup time than a normal Homebrew Ruby command allows and clients such as Cursor fail if they don't get a response quickly enough.

There are a few Ruby libraries available but, given how relatively simplistic the implementation is, it didn't feel worthwhile to use and vendor them.
